Alex.confusing: The Meowfia payout: the doubled "Grudge" bonus on a winning throw wasn't clear until the result, and it was unclear whether Farm stakes double too.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I bluffed my way out as a fake Turkey and the table eggsecuted Blair, the wrong Farm player. It earned me a doubled stake.
Alex.change: I'd add a way to verify claims. As it is, a lone Farm claim like Drew's "hugged" report is easy to turn into a scapegoat.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed Turkey but had visited Drew. Ellis caught it right away, and it put suspicion on me and Casey. I should have claimed an animal that visits someone and named a plausible target instead.

Blair.confusing: The final score breakdown was hard to follow: "bonus" and "kept" weren't explained, so I couldn't tell how kept cards and the 5-point wins were counted. Also, a confused dawn report gave me no way to know which information was wrong.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was fun: my Hawk visit gained an egg, which pinned Casey as Meowfia and let the table reason from a hard fact. Watching the stories contradict each other and then converge on Casey was satisfying.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about confusion, and show each player's score breakdown during the game rather than only at the end. That would make the scoring easier to follow.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw my 7 at Casey, who was Meowfia, but I should have thrown more cards at Alex, since Alex was also Meowfia and had been caught lying. I would have thrown higher cards at both Meowfia to bank more points.

Casey.confusing: How the Meowfia stake doubling worked, and whether Kookaburra or Falcon reports could be trusted given confusion and hugs.
Casey.fun: Round 1: winking Ellis mid-sentence, then steering the table into eggsecuting Blair for a big doubled payout.
Casey.change: Make the Sphinx and Mouser less self-incriminating, and give some way to check which visit claims are possible so lies are easier to catch.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I claimed Tit and said I visited Drew, which Ellis's Falcon and Drew's Kookaburra reports contradicted. I should have named Ellis or Drew as my visit in a way that fit what they were likely to say, or stayed vaguer.

Drew.confusing: The hug logic was the hardest part: a hug only tells you who visited a Floofer, not who the Floofer is, and I wrongly treated it as proof of the target's role. Also, I couldn't tell whether the Sphinx reveal from the Kookaburra was the animal or just a role.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when my Kookaburra named Casey as the Sphinx and the table had to decide whether to believe me. The conflicting Eagle, Falcon and Tit stories made the day feel like a real interrogation.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about what a role learned, so players aren't left guessing whether a revealed animal or role is the real information.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair because I assumed a hug meant Blair was the Floofer, when the hugger was actually Alex. I would instead have pressed Alex directly, since he was the one who had visited me and changed his story.

Ellis.confusing: How the Storyteller's stated nest-size changes interact with roles, and whether a Turkey or hugged visits show up in other animals' reports, was unclear.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when my Eagle report exposed Alex and Casey's lies, and the Round 3 reasoning that hugs pointed to Drew.
Ellis.change: Make Wink deaths less decisive. Killing a player who has just made a strong accusation takes away too much information.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I wrongly said Finley was the Floofer, based on my hug. I should have noticed that Drew said he visited me, and said so first.

Finley.confusing: Dawn reports were hard to trust, since confused and hugged results looked like lies, and claims from Owl, Kookaburra and Eagle were easy to contradict. Round 2's "Turkey doesn't see visitors" correction also confused which Farm claims were real.
Finley.fun: Round 1's Ellis Eagle callout, when I checked it against my own visit and the table turned on Alex and Casey, was the most satisfying read.
Finley.change: Publish each player's role in the day summary, or at least confirm which claims were tested by night actions, so Farm players aren't forced to guess at contradictions.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I winked Blair, a confirmed Farm Hawk, when Casey was already my partner and the wink hid nothing useful. I would instead have used the Wink later, or kept Blair alive as a credible witness to press Alex's Turkey lie.
